problem:
Describe the set $S={2,1,\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{4},...}$ using a constructive definition.

$$
S={{{field-1}}\,:\,n\in {{field-2}}}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
The given set contains the roots $x\in R$ of some quadratic polynomial $p(x).$

Since the polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-\sqrt{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=\sqrt{3},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2}) \\  & =2(x-(-\sqrt{3}))(x-\sqrt{3}) \\  & =2(x+\sqrt{3})(x-\sqrt{3}) \\  & =2({x}^{2}-\sqrt{3}x+\sqrt{3}x-(\sqrt{3})^{2}) \\  & =2({x}^{2}+0x-3) \\  & =2{x}^{2}+0x-6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express the given set as follows:

$$
{-\sqrt{3},\sqrt{3}}={x\in R\,:\,2{x}^{2}+0x-6=0}
$$
